fieldNotes.truckGate: Fully enclosed private import-DC campus. The south drop yard is reached by a single wrap-around pinch point at the building's west end (north campus drive -> around west wall -> south yard); the rest of the property is bounded by the building (N) and wooded/landscaped buffers (S, E). No public through-access. A barrier-arm/booth could not be positively resolved in satellite, but a bonded import DC of this class operates controlled truck entry - marked true at medium confidence.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No small staffed-booth structure (1-3 stall footprint) could be identified at any entrance pinch point in z19-z21 imagery; the only small structure near the SW gate area is yard equipment (a yellow dock ramp/container handler against the dock wall).
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Gate present without a visible guard booth -> implies kiosk / call-box / app check-in.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Continuous dock-door run along the entire ~600 m south wall with trailers backed in across the full length; clearly 50+ (estimate ~130 doors).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Dozens of trailers parked in marked drop stalls without tractors across the south yard; clearly 50+.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved aprons between the dock wall and the drop-yard rows provide internal queue/staging; inferred.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide paved yard aprons at the west wrap-around entry leave ample room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Single shared wrap-around entry pinch point inferred (entry/exit together); lane counts not directly resolvable.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Hawks Prairie / Lacey Gateway industrial park on the edge of Lacey, WA near I-5; large-warehouse cluster surrounded by woods, retention ponds and some residential - judged Rural per the small-town-industrial tiebreak.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter ring (building footprint + south drop yard) traced from z16 imagery ~ 62 acres; the building alone is the ~1.7M sq ft Target import warehouse.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: One contiguous import warehouse is the truck-operations facility; the adjacent warehouses N/S/E are separate properties in the same business park.
fieldNotes.streetView: Nearest Street View panos sit on the perimeter public roads set back behind wooded buffers (e.g. 47.0833,-122.7794 captured 2026-04); none directly faces the internal truck gate and pano_ids could not be retrieved without the Maps key, so hasCoverage is left false rather than inventing an id.
